rhn_librarian.text: Institute rules: no spitting, no swearing and no hats on the books. A penny a week out of every pay packet built this room, the library and the reading room.
The miners ran the place themselves. There was a committee, a treasurer, minutes. People think the valleys were all coal dust and hymns. They were also quite remarkably well organised.

Have a look at the framed notice by the shelves. It's about the Tredegar Medical Aid Society. A few pence a week and the whole family saw a doctor. A man called Bevan helped run it, and later copied it for the whole country.

rhn_reader.text: Shh. I'm on the last chapter of 'How Green Was My Valley'. Richard Llewellyn wrote it about a mining village, and there's a stern father in it who sings very well.
I'll tell you the secret of the Institute: it was warm. A reading room with a coal fire and no draught beats most things, and I include the pub.

then.text: Six flats. Four are let to people who grew up within a mile. One is mine. I lie awake sometimes and think about the pew I sat in, and then I go to sleep in the room that has the pulpit's window.
I put my plans in a drawer. They are still in the drawer. If the roof fund ever gives up, I will still be here, and I will still not be the villain.
Two flats in the old Sunday school and both let. I did them for less than I would have done the lot. Do not tell the bank.
Whatever Eirlys decides, I will be civil. It is only a building. It is only the building where I was baptised, but it is only a building.
Tell her I would sooner it was kept, if it could be. And tell her I cannot do it for love.

else.text: Kieran Rees. I do conversions. I was in Bethania's Sunday school until I was fourteen, and I did not like it much, and I would rather like it not to fall in.

Six flats, kept in the old shell with the front left as it is. I live in the valley and I know what it costs to rent here, and what it costs to buy. The lads I went to school with are in Cardiff because there was nothing for them here.
The chapel is not going to be a chapel for much longer: you can see it from the road. The choice is flats, or the roof coming in. Nobody is paying for the third thing.
I would give the choir a room. Not the room, a room. I know that is not the same.
Sorry, plans. Do not mind the drawings. I have been told to be gentle with the margins.

w55w_chorister.text: We rehearse here now, Thursdays and Saturdays. The Institute has a good heater and an acoustic like a wardrobe.
Elwyn says we will get used to it. Elwyn has said that about a great many things, and he has been right about most.
